the: A worn wooden signpost stands alone at a crossroads on a flat plain, one arm pointing forward, the neutral sky overhead. The post is painted white with a single black arrow. No destination is written on it — just the arrow, indicating direction without naming anything.
and: Two separate iron rings lie side by side on a stone surface, then a third ring links through both of them, forming a short chain. The rings are slightly tarnished gold. The scene is lit from above so the shadows show each loop clearly connected to the next.
to: A slender brass compass needle points steadily toward a distant doorway at the far end of a long stone corridor. The doorway glows faintly. The needle floats in midair at eye level, its tip aimed squarely at the threshold ahead.
a: A single smooth marble rests on the center of a wide empty table. It is clear glass with a pale blue swirl inside. Everything around it is bare. The marble is ordinary but distinct — one object, alone, set apart from nothing.
was: A half-melted candle sits in a puddle of its own hardened wax on a stone shelf, its flame now extinguished, a thin curl of smoke rising from the dark wick. The wax is ivory-colored and set solid. Shadows fill the background.
he: A silhouette of a male figure stands facing slightly left, solid dark blue against a pale grey background. His shoulders are broad, posture relaxed, hands at his sides. The figure is defined only by outline — no face, no clothing detail — just a clear, upright male shape.
she: A silhouette of a female figure stands facing slightly right, solid rose-pink against a pale cream background. Her posture is composed, hair gathered at the nape, dress hem brushing her knees. The figure is defined only by outline — clean edges, no face detail.
they: Three silhouettes stand side by side facing forward — one teal, one amber, one lavender — each a different height. They form a small group, shoulders nearly touching. The background is soft grey. No individual features are visible; the group reads as a unit.
it: A plain wooden box with a closed lid sits centered on a stone floor under a single overhead light. The box is unpainted, featureless, mid-sized. Nothing labels it. The flat light emphasizes the object's neutrality — it is simply a thing, waiting.
her: A small rose-pink scarf is draped over the back of a wooden chair. It is lightweight, slightly translucent, with delicate fringe at the ends. The chair is otherwise empty. The scarf curves gently, suggesting the recent presence of the person who left it.
said: A speech balloon made of carved stone floats just above an empty stone pedestal. The balloon is solid, not paper — its surface rough and permanent. Inside it a small lowercase cursive word-shape is engraved. The background is plain white.
you: A pointing finger extends from the left edge of the image directly toward the viewer, centered, as if pointing out of a painted canvas. The hand is rendered in warm ochre. The background behind the outstretched arm is a deep navy blue.
in: A small glowing lantern sits inside a dark cave alcove, nested within the rock. The lantern's amber light illuminates the curved stone walls around it. The opening of the alcove frames the lantern on three sides. A sense of enclosure and containment.
his: A battered leather satchel hangs from a hook on a plain wooden wall. Initials are pressed into the leather near the clasp. The bag is closed, worn with use, distinctly belonging to someone. Muted brown tones throughout.
with: Two iron keys hang on the same wooden peg, their bows touching. One key is slightly larger than the other. They are separate objects but occupy the same space, hanging together in quiet pairing.
lily: A young girl of about six with curly red hair and bright green eyes stands in a sunlit meadow holding a single white lily flower up to her nose. She wears a yellow dress with white trim. Her expression is curious and delighted.
that: A gyroscope spins steadily on a small pedestal, its inner ring tilted to one side. A slender pointing rod attached to the base angles toward the spinning ring, singling it out from several other objects placed nearby. The scene is lit from one side.
so: A set of brass scales is perfectly balanced, both pans level, holding equal weights. The scales stand on a dark wood table. Above one pan a single small sun-shape glows; the balance is complete, the consequence fulfilled.
day: A wide meadow scene at high noon, the sun positioned directly overhead in a cloudless blue sky. Long shadows fall straight down from a fence post and a tree at the edge of the field. The light is warm and even, everything clearly visible.
of: A large ceramic jar with a narrow neck sits beside a neat pile of spilled dried beans that have flowed from it. The beans form a small mound on the table surface. The relationship between container and contents is the subject.
but: An ornate iron gate stands open on the left side and firmly shut on the right side, the two halves meeting at the center with a heavy latch. The left path continues into green fields; the right path is blocked. The gate divides two possibilities.
had: An hourglass lies on its side on a wooden shelf, all its sand settled in the lower chamber, run completely through. The glass is pale amber-tinted. Dust motes float in a slant of light nearby. The moment of having is over.
on: A small brass figurine of a cat sits squarely on top of a thick stack of old leather-bound books. The stack is neat, the figurine perfectly centered. The scene is lit from the left, throwing the figurine's shadow down the side of the stack.
mom: A warm woman in her mid-thirties with dark brown hair pulled back in a loose bun wears a flour-dusted apron over a green shirt. She stands at a kitchen counter, looking over her shoulder with a gentle smile. A mixing bowl sits in front of her.
one: A single tall white candle stands upright in a plain holder on an otherwise completely bare dark wooden table. No other objects are present. The candle is lit, its flame small and steady. The surrounding darkness makes the single flame the only point of interest.
for: A neatly wrapped gift box tied with a satin ribbon sits at the edge of a table, its label tag turned toward the viewer but blank. The box is positioned as if placed there for a recipient who has not yet arrived.
very: A thermometer mounted on a wooden board shows its red liquid column risen far above the midpoint, nearly to the top. The top portion of the scale is marked with red hatching. The board is slightly worn but the thermometer is bright and clear.
there: A distant hilltop is visible at the end of a dirt path that stretches away from the viewer. A lone tree stands on the hilltop, silhouetted against a pale sky. The path leads clearly toward that far point, emphasizing distance and destination.
little: A tiny wooden toy chair sits in the center of a large empty tabletop. The chair is perfectly made — four legs, a back rail, a seat — but it is palm-sized. The vast surrounding surface emphasizes its smallness.
time: A large antique hourglass stands centered on a mahogany table, sand flowing slowly from the upper bulb to the lower. The glass is clear, the sand pale gold. The frame is dark brass. The flow of sand is the only motion.
i: A tall slender mirror stands upright, its frame simple dark wood. The glass reflects only the viewer — no room, no background, just a clear reflection of whoever stands before it. The mirror is perfectly polished.
happy: A child of about seven with tousled blond hair is mid-jump on a sunny lawn, arms flung wide, mouth open in a wide grin. Their shadow stretches below them. Dandelion seeds float in the air around them. The light is warm and golden.
is: An abacus with a single bead slid to the right side of its rod stands on a plain desk. All other rows are empty; just one bead is in position, present and accounted for. The frame is pale wood, the bead bright red.
not: A large red circle is painted on a white wall with a bold diagonal slash through it, the universal negation symbol. The wall is otherwise bare. The symbol is clean-edged and emphatic. Nothing else appears in the image.
big: A full-grown brown bear sits in the center of an open clearing, occupying most of the frame. Pine trees at the edge of the clearing are visibly shorter than the bear's shoulder. The bear is calm, seated, enormously present.
saw: A child of about eight with wide dark eyes stands at the edge of a tall wooden fence, hands gripping the top rail, peering over at something beyond. Their knuckles are white, their gaze intent. Sunlight hits the back of their head.
were: A row of five empty wooden chairs stands in a neat line on a stone floor, slight dust on the seats, one tilted slightly out of alignment. The chairs are plain ladder-back style. The room is bare. The people are gone.
play: Two young children race across a grassy yard, one chasing the other with arms outstretched, both mid-stride and laughing. A red ball is mid-bounce nearby. The afternoon sun is low, casting long playful shadows behind them.
once: An old leather-bound storybook lies open on a reading stand, its left page covered in faded script. The first line of text begins with a large ornate capital letter. A single candle burns nearby, casting warm light over the page.
are: A cluster of five different flowers — each a different color — stands in a clear glass vase on a windowsill. Each flower is distinct but they share the same water, the same light. Sunlight comes through the glass behind them.
their: A pair of identical small red backpacks hangs on two adjacent hooks on a wooden wall peg-rail. The hooks are next to each other. The backpacks are matching, signaling shared ownership. The wall is plain white.
wanted: A child of about five stands on tiptoe at a bakery display case, pressing both palms flat against the glass, staring at a single frosted cupcake on the other side. Their breath fogs the glass slightly. Their expression is one of pure longing.
upon: A stack of three flat river stones are piled one on top of the other on a mossy log, each stone balanced precisely on the one below. The stones are grey, smooth, and slightly different sizes. The image emphasizes layering and support.
them: Three small painted wooden figurines stand in a loose cluster on a shelf — each a different color but the same height. They face the same direction. A hand (cut off at the wrist) is visible at the edge of the frame, gesturing toward the group.
him: A baseball cap hangs on a hook at the end of a hallway, a worn jacket slung below it, work boots on the mat beneath. The arrangement is decidedly male. The light from a single bulb overhead is warm and focused on these items.
girl: A young girl of about eight with straight black hair and a yellow ribbon stands facing forward in a school yard, school bag at her feet. She wears a blue pinafore over a white shirt. Her expression is calm and open.
have: Two cupped hands hold a nest of small smooth stones — not releasing them, not offering them, simply holding. The hands are a child's, slightly dirty at the knuckles. The stones are pale grey. The image reads as possession and care.
be: A seedling pushes up through dark soil, its first two leaves just unfolding. The plant is tiny but upright. The soil is moist and dark around it. Soft light from above illuminates the pale green leaves. Potential, existence beginning.
can: A tin can with its lid fully removed stands upright, empty and open, its inside catching the light. The label has been torn away. The can is clean and shining. Its open top suggests capacity — the ability to hold.
ben: A boy of about nine with short sandy hair, freckles across his nose, and a striped green-and-white shirt. He holds a kite string in one hand, the diamond-shaped kite visible high above him in a pale blue sky. His expression is focused and pleased.
at: A plain wooden arrow mounted on a wall points at a small red dot painted at the center of a white target circle. The arrow is precise, the tip aligned exactly. The rest of the wall is blank.
up: A red balloon floats at the very top of the image, its string trailing downward and disappearing at the bottom edge. The sky around it is pale blue with no clouds. The balloon is round and vivid against the open sky.
tom: A stocky boy of about ten with dark brown hair cut bluntly and muddy knees stands beside a garden fence, grinning and holding up a large earthworm. He wears denim overalls over a red shirt. His expression is mischievous.
go: A green traffic light glows at the top of a metal pole at an empty intersection. The light is vivid and clear against a dark evening sky. The road ahead is empty and open. The amber and red lights below are unlit.
went: A pair of small muddy boot prints leads away from the viewer across a light-colored stone floor, the tracks diminishing in size as they go. The last print is barely visible. The footprints record motion already completed.
all: A large clear glass jar stands completely full of dried red beans, packed so tightly the beans press against every part of the glass. The lid is on. Nothing is missing. The jar sits on a plain white surface.
friends: Three children of similar age sit in a loose circle on a grassy hill, facing each other. One has red hair, one has black braids, one has blond curls. They are all laughing. A picnic blanket spreads beneath them.
we: Two pairs of small hands — one with dark skin, one with light skin — clasp together in the center of the image. The grip is easy and familiar, not formal. The arms disappear at the edges of the frame. Simple background.
when: An old brass alarm clock sits on a wooden bedside table, its single hand approaching twelve. The clock face is plain. On the table beside it a small bedside lamp is still on. The moment-before quality is the whole subject.
from: A river flows from a rocky mountain spring at the upper left of the image down toward a wide plain at the lower right. The water is clear at the source and widens as it goes. The origin and destination are both visible.
what: A question mark made of wrought iron stands upright on a stone pedestal in the center of an otherwise empty stone-walled room. The mark is large, well-formed, slightly rusty at the edges. A single spotlight hits it from above.
then: A row of five dominoes is shown mid-topple — the first three are already fallen, the fourth in mid-fall, the fifth still standing. The sequence reads left to right. The floor is plain wood.
back: A dirt path curves out of frame to the left and returns, rejoining the path at the bottom of the image from the right side. A single pair of footprints goes out and an identical pair returns. The path forms a loop.
too: A full teacup sits on a saucer beside a second, equally full teacup on the same saucer. Both cups are identical, both filled to the same level. No spoon, no extras. Two of exactly the same thing, side by side.
named: An adult hand holds a smooth flat river stone, and with a black marker is carefully writing a single word on its surface. The stone is white. The letters are being formed deliberately. A small pile of blank stones waits nearby.
loved: A faded photograph in a cracked frame shows a young woman smiling in a garden — the photo old, colors warm and soft. A fresh flower has been placed in front of the frame. The flower is vivid; the photograph is aged. The contrast says long devotion.
like: A child holds a mirror up to a sunflower, and the flower's reflection appears bright and crisp in the glass. The child's hand is in frame below. The flower and its reflection are nearly identical. A moment of clear resemblance.
smiled: A young woman's face is shown in three-quarter view, the corners of her mouth still slightly raised after a smile that has just passed. A soft warmth remains in her eyes. The expression is post-smile — the feeling settled in.
felt: An open hand lies palm-up, fingertips just touching the surface of still water. Rings of ripple radiate from each fingertip. The hand is relaxed. The contact has just been made and the sensation is complete.
fun: A group of three children are mid-splash in a shallow backyard pool on a bright summer afternoon. Water droplets hang in the air. All three faces are turned upward, mouths open in laughter. Towels lie forgotten on the grass.
asked: A young child with wide eyes looks up at a taller adult figure (cropped at the chest), one hand raised slightly in a gesture of question. The child's head is tilted to one side. Afternoon light comes through a window behind them.
could: A small wooden drawbridge is shown halfway raised, neither fully open nor fully closed. The gap in the middle is visible. The mechanism — chains and counterweights — is visible. It is poised at the moment of possibility.
looked: A boy's face is shown in profile, eyes focused on something to the right that is out of frame. His expression is attentive but neutral. The gaze is settled — he has already found what he was looking for. The looking is done.
around: A child stands at the center of a circular garden path, turning slowly, arms slightly out. The garden is full of flowers on all sides. The composition is circular, everything surrounding the figure at the middle.
timmy: A small boy of about five with a gap-toothed smile and large round glasses, wearing a bright orange knit sweater. He holds a toy train engine in both hands, lifting it toward the viewer proudly. His hair is dark and unruly.
do: A pair of hands is shown in mid-action assembling the pieces of a small wooden puzzle on a table. One piece is mid-placement, hovering just above its slot. The action is actively in progress, not yet finished.
out: A bright yellow rubber duck sits outside a bathtub on the tiled bathroom floor, slightly away from the tub's edge. The tub is visible in the background, filled with water. The duck has clearly been set outside, not inside.
help: A larger hand clasps the wrist of a smaller hand — a child's — and lifts it over a fence stile. The adult figure is partially visible at the top left. The child's feet are mid-step. The contact between the two hands is the center of the image.
did: A child's drawing in crayon is pinned to a corkboard. The drawing shows a simple house and tree. At the bottom, in a child's handwriting, is written a single checkmark. The task is complete — done, recorded.
see: A child crouches at the edge of a tide pool, face very close to the water, eyes open wide. Beneath the water's surface a small fish is visible. The child's expression is one of fresh discovery. The fish is clearly visible.
some: A bowl holds a mix of differently colored marbles — some red, some blue, some green. A small portion of them have been scooped to one side by a wooden spoon. Not all, not one — an intermediate handful scooped into view.
boy: A young boy of about seven with shaggy brown hair and scraped knees crouches at the edge of a muddy puddle, poking it with a stick. He wears sneakers and cargo shorts. His expression is one of focused curiosity.
would: A compass rose is shown on a parchment map, its needle hovering between two directions — not pointing with finality, but suspended in potential. A faint dotted line extends from the needle's tip in two directions.
as: A sundial and a clock face are shown side by side on a stone garden wall. Both display the same time — the shadow of the sundial and the clock hands align exactly. The comparison is the subject.
make: A craftsperson's hands are shown pressing clay into a mold on a wooden workbench. The clay is mid-shape, impressions forming. Tools are laid out nearby. The act of forming something new from raw material is central.
says: A figure at a podium is mid-sentence, mouth open, one hand raised palm-out in a speaking gesture. The listener's back is visible in the foreground. The speaker is mid-delivery — the words are currently leaving his mouth.
mommy: A young woman with long brown hair kneels on a playroom floor, arms wide open, face lit with warmth. A small toddler is mid-run toward her arms. The room has toy blocks and a soft mat. Morning light fills the room.
away: A dandelion stem stands in a field, already half-gone — seeds floating away to the right on a breeze, the puff only partially intact. The seeds drift in a loose trail toward the right edge of the image. The leaving is underway.
together: Two children sit under the same tree, shoulders touching, each reading the same large picture book held between them. Their heads both tilt toward the book's center. The tree canopy above them creates a shared circle of shade.
ran: A child's sneakers are visible mid-stride, blurred from motion, both feet off the ground simultaneously. The ground beneath is a paved path. The blur on the shoes and the gap between feet and ground capture the sprint's peak.
made: A small clay pot sits finished on a potter's wheel that has stopped spinning. The pot is formed and firm, its shape set. The artist's hands are visible at the sides, still and satisfied. Clay residue on the wheel. The making is over.
want: A child stands at a bakery window, pressing their nose against the glass, eyes fixed on a single frosted cupcake on a rotating display stand inside. The cupcake is close but unreachable. The child's longing is the whole image.
started: A runner is shown at the very first stride out of the starting blocks — one foot just pushing off, the other still on the block, body still low. The track stretches ahead. This is the very first instant of the race.
something: A wrapped parcel sits on a doorstep, addressed but not yet opened. Brown paper, rough twine. The parcel's shape is irregular — it contains an object that is not yet revealed. The mystery of its contents is the subject.
park: A cheerful children's playground in a green park on a sunny afternoon. A bright red slide, a yellow climbing frame, and a set of swings occupy the center. Two children play on the equipment; a park bench sits nearby under a leafy tree.
sad: A young child of about four sits alone on a wooden step, knees pulled to their chest, head bowed. A dropped ice cream cone lies melted on the pavement nearby. The child's shoulders are curved inward. Soft grey afternoon light.
new: A freshly unwrapped object — a shiny bright red bicycle — stands alone in a garage, its plastic wrapping torn away and piled to one side. The bicycle is pristine, tires clean, chrome sparkling. The newness radiates from it.
home: A small white house with green shutters and a red front door sits at the end of a short garden path lined with flowers. Warm light glows from inside through the front windows. Smoke curls softly from the chimney. Late afternoon.
again: A boomerang is shown at the far end of its arc, turning back toward the thrower (whose arm is visible at the left edge). The boomerang is mid-return, tracing a curved dotted line back to where it began.
found: A child is crouched beside a garden wall, hand outstretched, discovering a lost toy car half-buried in the soil. Their expression is bright with recognition. The small red car is half-unearthed, soil still on it.
who: A silhouette of a figure stands in a doorway, completely backlit, features impossible to make out. The light behind them is bright. The doorframe defines their outline but reveals nothing of their identity. The image sits with the question.
put: A hand is shown placing a single smooth stone precisely on top of a cairn — a careful, deliberate placement. The hand is steady. The stone is just making contact with the top of the stack. The act of placement is the subject.
tim: A tall thin boy of about twelve with wire-rimmed glasses and a navy blue turtleneck sweater stands reading a thick book, holding it in both hands, slightly absorbed. He has light brown hair parted to one side, and his posture is very upright.
playing: A group of three young children are in the middle of a game of tag on a grass lawn, one reaching out to tag another, all in mid-stride. Their faces show pure engagement. A rubber ball lies untouched to one side — they've abandoned it for the chase.
bird: A small bright blue songbird perches on a thin brown branch against a pale grey sky. Its beak is slightly open in mid-song. The feathers are detailed — cobalt on the wings, white at the breast. The branch is bare of leaves.
liked: A child holds a picture they've just drawn, tilting it slightly to look at it from a distance, a quiet satisfied expression on their face. The drawing is simple but finished. The appreciation is settled and done.
things: A wooden crate holds a jumble of assorted small objects — a spool of thread, a smooth stone, a wooden top, a small key, a seashell, a thimble. The objects are varied, mundane, and unrelated. The crate contains a collection of things.
other: Two identical wooden doors stand side by side in a plain wall. The left one is open; the right one is closed. A figure is stepping toward the closed one. The unchosen open door is the focus — the other option.
no: A hand is shown palm-outward in a firm stop gesture, fingers together, wrist straight, the gesture emphatic. The hand is centered against a plain red background. No other elements. The gesture is clear and final.
got: A child reaches up to a high shelf and wraps both hands around a small wooden box, having just pulled it down. The box is in their grip, the reach complete. Their expression is one of quiet satisfaction. The getting is done.
dad: A tall man in his late thirties wearing a plaid flannel shirt kneels on a garage floor beside a bicycle, a wrench in his hand. Grease marks his forearm. He looks over his shoulder with a good-natured grin. Tool kit open beside him.
came: A trail of wet boot prints on a wooden floor leads from a front door (still slightly ajar, rain visible outside) toward the interior of a room. The prints are fresh and dark. The door's direction and the prints tell the full story of arrival.
decided: A hand hovers over two paths drawn on a map laid flat on a table. A pencil just touches the left-hand path, marking the chosen route. The other path remains untouched. The moment of commitment is captured — the other option behind.
look: A child stands on tiptoe at the rim of a stone well, shading their eyes with one hand, peering down into the dark water below. The action is active and present — the looking is happening now, not yet resolved.
excited: A young child of about six bounces on the balls of their feet, fists clenched at their sides, eyes wide and bright, mouth open in a gape of anticipation. Behind them, balloons are partially visible. The energy is barely contained.
friend: Two children of about eight walk side by side on a path, shoulders bumping lightly, one whispering something to the other. The listener's expression is warm amusement. Their postures mirror each other. Late afternoon light behind them.
scared: A young child of about six stands at the top of a dark staircase leading into a basement. The light at the bottom is faint. The child grips the doorframe tightly, leaning back slightly, one foot lifted. Wide eyes.
this: A hand points at a single object — a smooth round stone on a table — singling it out from a small row of similar stones. The pointing finger's tip nearly touches the chosen stone. All other stones are in soft focus.
man: A broad-shouldered figure in a dark coat stands with their back to the viewer, looking out over an open field at dusk. The silhouette is tall and male. His hands are in his coat pockets. The field stretches quietly ahead.
your: An open mailbox on a suburban post shows a single white envelope inside, address face-up, a name clearly written on it (the name itself not readable). The flag is down — the letter is waiting for its owner.
down: A red ball is shown at the bottom of a long wooden ramp, having come to rest against a small block stopper at the base. Its track down the ramp is traced by a faint streak above it. The motion is over, the object settled.
good: A sunlit kitchen windowsill holds a row of home-baked bread loaves, cooling on a wire rack. The crusts are golden and perfect. A worn blue cloth sits neatly folded beside them. The image radiates warmth, competence, simple rightness.
will: A seedling in a terracotta pot is shown with a small painted wooden sign tucked into the soil beside it: a single upward arrow. The seedling is still tiny. The arrow promises growth to come. Warm light from the right.
sam: A cheerful girl of about eight with short curly black hair and bright brown eyes stands at a chalkboard, chalk in hand, having just drawn a large star with five neat points. She wears a striped purple shirt. Her grin is confident.
my: A child's hand rests protectively on top of a small battered notebook, pulling it slightly toward themselves from the edge of a table. Their name is written in crayon on the notebook's cover. The gesture is possessive and definitive.
an: A single apple sits alone at the center of an otherwise empty white plate on a white tablecloth. The apple is red, slightly imperfect, with a stem and a single small leaf. It is singled out from everything — one, indefinite.
dog: A golden retriever sits upright on a wooden porch, tail blurred in a wag, mouth open in a panting grin. Its fur catches afternoon sunlight. A well-chewed tennis ball sits at its front paws. The dog looks directly at the viewer.
me: A child's drawing shows a single stick figure at the center of a white page, surrounded by a careful pencil-drawn circle. The figure is labeled with an arrow pointing to it from the word 'me' in wobbly handwriting. The rest of the page is blank.
anna: A girl with straight blonde hair cut at the chin, pale blue eyes, seven years old, wearing a red pinafore over a white blouse. She stands with hands clasped behind her back, a small woven basket looped over one elbow.
get: A hand reaches toward a brass doorknob, fingers just touching the surface, the arm extended at full stretch. The background is plain cream, the doorknob polished and catching a warm point of light.
find: A magnifying glass held over a patch of scattered small objects — a thimble, a coin, a folded scrap of paper — one object circled by the lens's bright rim. The background is dark navy, the found object glowing slightly.
toys: A low wooden shelf crowded with small objects: a painted wooden top, a cloth rabbit, a set of stacking rings, and a tin trumpet, each casting a short shadow. Warm lamp-light falls from the upper left, colors bright against pale pine.
always: An hourglass with both chambers full, grains of sand frozen mid-fall, a looping arrow etched around the outside of the glass indicating it will be flipped and continue without end. The hourglass sits on a stone plinth against a deep indigo background.
took: A closed hand lifted slightly from an empty flat surface, a single small coin pressed between the thumb and forefinger, the surface below showing a faint round impression where the coin rested. Neutral grey background, strong overhead light.
about: A compass rose drawn on aged parchment, the needle pointing not to north but circling loosely, indicating approximate direction rather than exact. Around it small marks suggest a subject being outlined without being pinned down.
max: A stocky boy with short dark-red hair and a wide grin, eleven years old, wearing a grey athletic jacket with orange trim. He stands with arms crossed, one eyebrow raised, a soccer cleat tucked under one arm.
didn't: A smooth blank signpost stands at a crossroads, the arm pointing in one direction marked with a bold red X, the path beneath it clearly visible but deliberately uncrossed. Grey overcast sky, muted earth tones.
outside: A view through an open door frame: bright green grass, a pale blue sky, and a tree visible at the edge, the interior side of the frame showing dark wood and a coat hook. The threshold is clearly lit from the exterior.
tree: A single broad-canopied oak stands centered in the image, its trunk thick and furrowed, branches spreading wide against a clear sky. Late-afternoon light catches the upper leaves in gold while the lower trunk rests in cool shade.
more: A ceramic bowl already filled with glossy dark cherries, and a hand pouring additional cherries from a small colander, the overflow beginning to mound above the rim. Clean white background, strong side lighting.
how: An open leather-bound manual lies flat, one page showing a numbered diagram with arrows pointing step-by-step from a raw lump of clay on the left to a finished pot on the right. The page is yellowed at the edges.
thought: A single glowing filament suspended inside a glass bell jar, shaped loosely like a question mark, casting soft amber light onto the dark surface beneath. The bell jar has a small brass collar at its base.
sorry: A small hand-lettered card on cream paper reads nothing — instead shows a wilted violet laid flat beside it, a faint smudge on one corner suggesting a tear. Muted lavender background, soft even lighting.
take: An open hand presented palm-up beneath a glass marble, the marble balanced in the center of the palm, the fingers beginning to close around it. Plain white background, sharp downward light.
old: A pair of worn leather boots with cracked soles and laces replaced by fraying twine, leaning against one another as if too tired to stand upright. The leather is creased with deep lines, colour faded to a dusty tan.
it's: A small label tied to the neck of a glass bottle with a thin string, the label showing an arrow pointing at the bottle itself and a simplified equals sign. White background, bold black linework on the label.
inside: A cross-section view of a small wooden chest, the lid propped open to reveal a velvet-lined interior holding a single pearl, the external wood grain contrasting with the smooth crimson lining within. Side lighting.
special: A single gold-foil star sticker placed exactly in the center of a plain white card, the star slightly raised from the surface and catching light on each point. The surrounding card is completely unmarked, emphasizing the star's singularity.
knew: A head silhouette in dark charcoal, profile facing left, with a single lit lantern inside the skull area, the glow visible through the forehead. The lantern flame is steady, not searching — already alight. Dark background.
every: An abacus with every bead slid fully to the left side, all rows completed, the frame casting a neat shadow on cream paper. The beads alternate red and white, every column accounted for.
don't: A raised open palm facing outward — a clear stop gesture — against a plain red background. The fingers are together, the thumb extended slightly, the gesture centered and unambiguous.
toy: A small painted wooden horse on wheels, red with a yellow mane, sitting alone on a smooth wooden floor. A short length of white string is tied to a loop at its nose, trailing forward.
